players.product: Apple Silicon (A19 / A19 Pro, M5) — leading-edge logic on TSMC N2/N3

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 (December quarter) headline results - 'our best-ever quarter with $143.8 billion in revenue, up 16% from a year ago and exceeding our expectations'. iPhone all-time revenue record of $85.3 billion, up 23% year over year, 'driven by the iPhone 17 family' ('The demand for iPhone was simply staggering'); Services all-time record $30 billion, up 14%; Mac $8.4 billion, down 7% (difficult compare against the year-ago M4 MacBook Pro, Mac Mini and iMac launches); iPad $8.6 billion, up 6% (M5-powered iPad Pro and A16-powered iPad); wearables, home and accessories $11.5 billion, down 2% (constraints on AirPods Pro 3). Company gross margin 48.2% (above the high end of the guidance range, up 100 basis points sequentially on favorable mix and leverage); products gross margin 40.7% (up 450 basis points sequentially); services gross margin 76.5%. Operating expenses $18.4 billion, up 19% on increased R&D. Diluted EPS $2.84, up 19%; record operating cash flow $53.9 billion. Greater China up 38% year over year (best iPhone quarter in history there). Installed base more than 2.5 billion active devices. December tariff cost landed at roughly the $1.4 billion outlined. Cook: iPhone gained share in December, and Mac gained share for full calendar year 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: $143.8 billion revenue (up 16%); iPhone $85.3 billion (up 23%); gross margin 48.2%; EPS $2.84

quarterly_data.signal: Apple Silicon as the AI platform. Cook: Apple products are 'far and away the best platforms in the world for AI. That's in no small part because of the extraordinary power and performance of Apple Silicon.' The M5-powered 14-inch MacBook Pro 'takes a huge leap in AI performance thanks to the next-generation GPU architecture and a faster neural engine'; iPad growth was 'driven by the M5-powered iPad Pro and the A16-powered iPad'. Cook: 'the majority of users on enabled iPhones are actively leveraging the power of Apple Intelligence' (dozens of features, available in 15 languages). Enterprise pull: AstraZeneca 'is rolling out over 5,000 M5-powered iPad Pros to its pharmaceutical sales team to take advantage of AI capabilities, including Apple Intelligence'; Snowflake 'has deployed over 9,000 Mac devices company-wide'. The AI-capable share of the installed base is 'a growing number' (CFO declined to give a figure).
quarterly_data.figure: over 5,000 M5-powered iPad Pros (AstraZeneca); over 9,000 Mac devices (Snowflake)

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: A LEADING-EDGE NODE SHORTAGE GATES THE MARCH QUARTER. Cook: 'we exited December with very lean channel inventory due to that staggering level of demand. And based on that, we're in a supply chase mode to meet the very high levels of customer demand. We are currently constrained and at this point, it's difficult to predict when supply and demand will balance. The constraints that we have are driven by the availability of the advanced nodes that our SoCs are produced on. And at this time, we're seeing less flexibility in the supply chain than normal.' Asked why Apple is constrained (the analyst framed it as advanced packaging), Cook named the node: 'it's the advanced nodes that we, like three nanometer to be specific, where our SOCs are the latest SOCs are produced on is what is gating the Q2 supply', 'a direct result of the 23% growth' far outstripping internal estimates, with 'more limited flexibility in the supply chain for some period of time'. The March-quarter revenue outlook of 13% to 16% 'comprehends our best estimates of constrained iPhone supply during the quarter'. Cook declined to comment on supply beyond Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: 'three nanometer' advanced nodes gating Q2 supply; March-quarter revenue outlook of 13% to 16% includes constrained iPhone supply

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: FIRST READ ON THE MEMORY COST CYCLE. Cook: 'memory had a minimal impact on Q1. So the December gross margin. We do expect it to be a bit more of an impact to the Q2 gross margin and that was comprehended in the outlook of 48 to 49%... we do continue to see market pricing for memory increasing significantly. As always, we'll look at a range of options to deal with that.' Asked whether long-term agreements or spot buying is the answer for memory: 'It's a range, and so I don't want to get more specific than that. I mean, there are different levers that we can push, and who knows how successful they'll be'. Asked whether raising prices is a lever: 'I wouldn't want to speculate on that one.' CFO: the March gross margin guide is similar to the December level, with favorable services mix partly offset by a seasonal loss of leverage.
quarterly_data.figure: memory impact minimal in Q1, 'a bit more' in Q2 within the 48 to 49% gross margin outlook

quarterly_data.signal: March-quarter (Q2 FY2026) outlook, assuming tariff rates and policies in effect as of the call: total company revenue to grow 13% to 16% year over year (including constrained iPhone supply); services revenue growth similar to the December-quarter rate; gross margin between 48-49%; operating expenses between $18.4 billion and $18.7 billion (higher R&D year over year); OI&E around $100 million; tax rate around 17.5%. CFO: no particular product comp issue for March - 'continuation of the strong cycle we're seeing subject to constraints'.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue growth 13% to 16%; gross margin 48-49%; opex between $18.4 billion and $18.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: GOOGLE BECOMES THE FOUNDATION FOR APPLE'S MODELS. Cook: 'we are also collaborating with Google to develop the next generation of Apple foundation models. This will help power future Apple intelligence features, including a more personalized Siri coming this year.' 'We basically determined that Google's AI technology would provide the most capable foundation for Apple Foundation Models... We'll continue to run on the device and run-in private cloud compute.' Terms undisclosed ('we're not releasing the details of that'); 'you should think of what is going to power the personalized version of Siri as a collaboration with Google.' Compute: on-device and private cloud compute are both important ('we don't see it as an either-or'); on data center capacity for Siri, Cook: 'we've done the sort of the best job that we can do, and I've and either have or are putting capacity in for it.' Apple is 'shipping servers to power Apple Intelligence from our new manufacturing facility in Houston.' CFO: CapEx follows a hybrid model - on tooling and data centers Apple leverages 'a combination of first and third-party capacity'; CapEx 'can be volatile', and December-quarter results included CapEx for the private cloud compute environment built out last year.

US silicon supply chain progress under the commitment 'to invest $600 billion over four years in vital industries like advanced manufacturing, silicon engineering, and artificial intelligence': Apple continues 'to advance the development of an end-to-end silicon supply chain across the country, sourcing 20 billion US chips in 2025'; 'We're working with Micron, which broke ground on a new advanced chip packaging and test facility'; through the advanced manufacturing program Apple is 'working with Corning in Kentucky to make 100% of cover glass for iPhone and Apple Watch'; servers for Apple Intelligence now ship from the new Houston manufacturing facility; the program supports 'nearly half a million jobs with thousands of suppliers across all 50 states'.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 billion US chips sourced in 2025; $600 billion over four years

quarterly_data.signal: In-house silicon as a margin and roadmap lever. Cook: 'Apple silicon has just been an incredible game-changer for us. Starting with iPhone and then on iPad and, of course, the Mac as of a few years ago. And so we believe it's a game-changer and a major advantage.' CFO Parekh: Apple has been 'investing in core technologies like our own silicon and our own modem'; these 'do provide opportunities for cost savings' as well as differentiation and 'more control of our roadmap', and 'we are seeing... investments in our core technologies impacting... gross margin in a positive way.'
